title: Simulate Two-Phase Render and Commit Pipeline
subtopicTitle: Render Phase vs Commit Phase Mechanics
concept: Separation of VDOM Calculation and DOM Mutation
problemStatement: Implement `createUpdatePipeline()` that splits updates into two distinct phases: `renderPhase(components)` which computes DOM changes without touching the DOM, and `commitPhase(changes, targetDOM)` which applies all DOM mutations synchronously.
interviewTrap: Directly modifying the DOM during the render phase causes partial, broken UI states if the render gets aborted.

testCases.name: Calculates mutations in render phase without executing commit
testCases.testFn: const p = createUpdatePipeline(); return p.renderPhase([{ action: 'INSERT', id: '1', content: 'A' }, { action: 'UPDATE', id: '2', content: 'B' }]);

testCases.name: Flushes all staged mutations synchronously during commit
testCases.testFn: const p = createUpdatePipeline(); p.renderPhase([{ action: 'INSERT', id: '1', content: 'Hello' }, { action: 'UPDATE', id: '2', content: 'World' }]); return p.commitPhase();

testCases.name: Clears mutation buffer after commit
testCases.testFn: const p = createUpdatePipeline(); p.renderPhase([{ action: 'INSERT', id: '1', content: 'x' }]); p.commitPhase(); return p.commitPhase();

details.name: Calculates mutations in render phase without executing commit
Flushes all staged mutations synchronously during commit

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Simulating a complete Two-Phase Render and Commit Pipeline shows how React computes an effect list during render, and then executes synchronous DOM mutations and lifecycle commits in the commit phase.
stepByStepWalkthrough: - Traverse component tree, compute new virtual representation, and diff against current state.
- Accumulate mutation flags (`Placement`, `Update`, `Deletion`) onto fiber nodes without touching the real DOM.
- Synchronously iterate through fibers with effect flags.
- Flip double buffer root pointer: `root.current = workInProgress`.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In `packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberCommitWork.js`, `commitMutationEffects` mutates the DOM tree synchronously in one uninterrupted batch. This ensures the browser never renders an inconsistent intermediate UI state.

complexity.time: O(N) render diffing + O(M) commit mutations where M is number of changed fibers.

edgeCasesHandled: Render phase can abort without affecting DOM if work is canceled.
Commit phase executes in strict sub-phase order.
Root alternate pointer flips atomically at the conclusion of commit.

specifications: Dan Abramov: Component Lifecycle / Render vs Commit Phases chart
verifiedRules: Commit phase is synchronous and un-interruptible.
DOM mutations occur exclusively within commitMutationEffects.
